I don't know of an environment variable that sets a pass-rate threshold. The retrieved documents don't name one.

The quality-gate examples hardcode the threshold in the shell script rather than reading it from an environment variable. For example: "if (( $(echo "$PASS_RATE < 95" | bc -l) )); then" [promptfoo/site/docs/integrations/ci-cd.md]

The docs also show a built-in option that fails the run on any test failure, not on a pass-rate threshold: "npx promptfoo@latest eval --fail-on-error" [promptfoo/site/docs/integrations/ci-cd.md]

The environment-variables table in the command-line docs may list relevant variables, but the retrieved excerpts cut off before the rows, so I can't confirm whether any of them controls a pass-rate threshold. Checking the full table in "promptfoo/site/docs/usage/command-line.md" would settle it.
